items: Transcripts can follow Backup Track (the browser extension). Tick Follow Backup Track in the player bar and the recording here, its picture and its lit word move with the site you are transcribing on, so you can see who is speaking. The switch only appears when the extension is installed.
Reader: OCR… reads scanned pages and pictures so you can search and copy their text. It makes a new PDF and tells you, page by page, how sure it was. It is machine reading: check names and numbers.

Reader: Redact now works correctly on pages that are stored sideways or upside down. Before this version, a blacked-out word on such a page could stay readable. If you redacted a turned page earlier, check that copy again.
Reader: Pages, Redact and OCR are together under Tools.
Transcripts has a Legal mode (the § Legal button). Type a short code such as ;ina and it becomes the standard wording with the time, or pick from Insert.
Exhibits propose the next number and build an exhibit index and a witness index by themselves.
Alt + 1 to 9 set the speaker; examination headings set up Q and A.
Presets for US company style, US court, US deposition, South Africa and the UK. Nothing is ever inserted or guessed for you.
When you forget songs in Privacy and storage, a Player that is open elsewhere drops them at once instead of still showing them.
Easier to use with the keyboard: menus and dialogs take the keyboard and give it back, every control shows where you are, and in the Cutter F6 moves between controls (Tab still plays and pauses).
Easier to read: faint text is darker, and boxes have clearer edges.
Works better on a phone: nothing runs off the side, and buttons are finger-sized.
Studio: the top bar wraps to a second line on smaller screens instead of pushing Export off the edge, and the tempo label no longer blocks clicks.

Transcripts asks what a transcript is for. Paid or client work uses Mixtape's own recogniser. Personal can use Rev's Reverb through a helper on your computer; Rev's licence allows that for personal use only, and the transcript says so.
The Reader now opens Word, Markdown, plain text, RTF, OpenDocument, ebooks (.epub) and screenplays (.fountain) in a comfortable reading view.
Pages…: turn, delete, reorder, merge, extract and split the pages of a PDF, with Undo.
Redact…: black out words or areas in a PDF. The words are removed, not covered, and the new file is checked before you can save it.
Every tool now has a way back to Mixtape's home page, where Privacy and storage also lives.
When Mixtape has been updated while you have it open, a small notice tells you and lets you reload when it suits you. It never reloads by itself.
Press ? in any tool to see its keys. The Player and the Reader now have a keys list too.
The first time you open a tool, a short welcome points at where to start. You can skip it, and bring it back from the keys list.
If something goes wrong, Mixtape says so in plain words and tells you what to do next. The technical detail stays on your device.
A home page shows all five tools and what each is for.
Privacy and storage shows everything Mixtape keeps on this device, backs it all up to one file, restores it, and can forget it.
Mixtape no longer connects to any other website. Its fonts and the speech recogniser are now part of the app itself.
Studio: a round of fixes so that nothing is lost when storage is blocked or a save fails.
Cutter: “Forget everything on this device” (under Keys and tips) removes everything the Cutter keeps in this browser. Files you saved and your library are not touched.
Cutter: a round of fixes.
Player: if a favourite, a playlist or a song could not be saved or removed, the Player now tells you instead of carrying on as if it had worked.
Transcripts: a file saved from a recording you marked sensitive says so in its name and at its top.
Transcripts: a correction you were half-way through typing is never dropped.
Transcripts: after a pause, Play picks up 10 seconds earlier so you can find your place. Back jumps 10 seconds, forward 5.
Fixes across all the tools so that nothing is lost, and nothing is sent anywhere, by accident.
Reader: every change is saved into the file as you make it. Undo takes a change back, and “Back to original” restores the file as you opened it.
Cutter: when you join files, you choose whether to save the list of where each clip begins.
Cutter: a joined file comes with a list of where each clip begins and ends.
Cutter: joining a hundred files at once now works.
New tool: the Reader. Open PDFs, highlight and add notes, fill in forms and sign, all offline.
Cutter: the back and forward keys jump 3 seconds unless you choose another step.
Cutter: Tab plays and pauses and Shift + Tab goes back, as in Transcripts. The arrow keys move back and forward, and change the volume.
An installed Mixtape still opens its saved pages when the website answers with an error.
